subject: Pilot billing: rounding behavior, long-context trimming, and minimums
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Kelly Park <kelly.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot billing: rounding behavior, long-context trimming, and minimums

Hi Kelly,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great to see the ingestion demo take shape. I promised a short note on how billing will behave for the pilot so procurement can review:

High level (pilot-friendly):
- We meter per-token for both input and output. Tokens are counted at the model boundary after our tokenizer.
- Billing quantum: charges are rounded up to the nearest 100-token quantum for burst pricing only; baseline streaming/low-latency calls are still per-token in the meter but subject to a 50-token minimum per request to avoid micro-billing noise.
- Long-context handling: when a request includes >64k tokens of historical context, we automatically trim prefix context per your retention policy; trimming does not reduce the token count for the currently generated tokens but avoids paying for stale KV cache shots.
- Minimums & pilot cap: for pilots under 3 months we can apply a monthly cap and a one-time onboarding credit to cover warmup inefficiencies.

I'm attaching a short MAP (pilot-pricing-draft.xlsx) with a worked example using your expected 12k token/day profile. Two quick asks:
1) Can procurement confirm whether you need per-call breakdowns on the invoice (we can provide token-level CSVs)?
2) Would you prefer 100-token quantum for all charges, or just for bursts above 10k tokens/min?

If it helps, I can loop in Finance to propose a billing language tweak for the pilot SOW.

Best,
Dylan

--

Dylan —

Thanks for this summary, super helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/engineering after reviewing the sheet:

1) Rounding: The 100-token quantum for bursts seems reasonable, but we need clarity on how consecutive small calls are aggregated. If our app sends 10 back-to-back calls each with 30 tokens within 2s, will those be billed as 10x50-minimums, aggregated into a single quantum, or something else?

2) Minimums: The 50-token per-request minimum could penalize our microservice endpoints which often send 1-2 short prompts per user action. Is there a aggregation window or session-level smoothing we can rely on?

3) Long-context trimming: Your note about prefix trimming is good. We also need to understand whether trimming is deterministic (i.e., we can calculate pre-charge footprint) or happens post-hoc during runtime and is invisible on invoices.

4) Pilot cap: We appreciate the cap proposal — procurement will need a concrete dollar amount and what the cap covers (e.g., tokens only, or tokens + compute egress).

Can you put together a short explainer that maps our three traffic patterns (microservice short prompts, long conversation threads, and async batch inference) to how charges would be counted and rounded? Procurement is on a Thursday cadence for approvals so a Friday delivery would be great.

Thanks,
Kelly Park
Director, Clinical Product
Acme Health
kelly.park@acmehealth.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Pilot billing: rounding behavior, long-context trimming, and minimums

Team — forwarding Acme's follow-ups. Need a concise position for Friday:

Summary of asks from procurement:
- How back-to-back small calls are aggregated (they want to avoid paying 10x50 for 10 calls within a short window).
- Whether the per-request 50-token floor can be smoothed at session-level or by a 2-second aggregation window.
- Clarify determinism of prefix trimming and invoice visibility.
- Define a dollar cap for a 2-month pilot and what it covers.

My suggested answers (draft):
- Aggregation policy: we perform a short aggregation window (2 seconds) at the router level for identical session keys; requests within that window are bundled for charging into a single meter event and then rounded according to the applicable quantum. This currently applies to Hosted API and Dedicated; Private installs can opt-in to a similar router behavior but may need config changes.
- 50-token floor: propose we waive per-request minimum for any session that exceeds 200 tokens of cumulative activity in a rolling 1-minute window; effectively that smooths microservice traffic.
- Trimming: trimming is deterministic if you pin retention policy in the request metadata (we return a post-request footprint in the token CSV so you can reconcile).
- Pilot cap: propose $8,000/mo cap for the first two months covering tokens and outbound egress. Onboarding credit: $2,000 one-time.

Questions for Finance/Legal: is $8k/month reasonable for the pilot (their projected daily usage in the spreadsheet ~12k tokens/day)? Any objections to making the 2s aggregation configurable in the SOW?

Thanks — I can take this to Kelly once we have sign-off.

Best,
Dylan

Hi Kelly —

Appreciate the detailed questions. We've reviewed with Finance and Ops and can offer the following concrete terms for the 60-day pilot:

1) Aggregation & rounding
- Router-level aggregation: requests with the same session key arriving within a 2-second window will be aggregated into a single meter event.
- Quantum: aggregated meter events are rounded up to the nearest 100-token quantum for burst billing only. Individual non-aggregated low-latency calls will be billed per-token but subject to a soft 50-token minimum which can be waived by the session-smoothing rule below.

2) Session smoothing rule (to protect microservices)
- If a session accumulates >200 tokens within any rolling 60s window, the per-request 50-token minimum will be waived for calls in that window and charges will be computed on the true token count (post-aggregation).

3) Long-context trimming and auditability
- Trimming is deterministic when you set retention flags in the call (we provide an SDK param to pin prefix-slice policy).
- We will include a token CSV post-call and a daily reconciliation CSV for the pilot that shows: request_id, session_key, tokens_input, tokens_output, trimmed_prefix_tokens, billed_tokens. That should give your finance folks enough to audit invoicing.

4) Pilot cap & credits
- Cap: $8,000/month for the two-month pilot (covers tokens and standard outbound egress; excludes paid third-party connectors).
- One-time onboarding credit: $2,000 applied on first invoice to cover warm-up inefficiencies.

Next steps:
- I attached an updated MAP (MAP_v1.pdf) with the examples mapped to your three traffic patterns and the final numbers.
- If that looks good, I'll send a short SOW snippet for procurement and a DocuSign link to accept the pilot terms.

Let me know if you want a 15-min call tomorrow with our Head of Finance (Kimberly) to run through the CSV export format.

Best,
Dylan
